newsitem.title: USA: U.S. bomb plot suspect surrenders, police say.
newsitem.headline: U.S. bomb plot suspect surrenders, police say.

text.p: Kevin Robinson, suspected of ordering a series of bombings in a northern California town to disrupt his trial on drug charges, surrendered to police on Monday, police said.
"He did in fact surrender and he is in custody," said Bill Powell, a police spokesman in Vallejo that has been hit by two bombings in the last 10 days.

Robinson is the fourth suspect held in connection with two bomb blasts that damaged a courthouse and a bank in the town, 35 miles (50 km) northeast of San Francisco. All face conspiracy and explosives charges.
Police had issued an arrest warrant for Robinson, 29, who they said should be considered armed and dangerous.
Powell said Robinson's attorney made the arrangements for his surrender to Vallejo police.
Police said they believed Robinson hired two men already in custody to carry out the bombings to disrupt his trial on drugs charges that was due to start in a nearby town on Monday.
